Subject: Program credit escrow, transferability, and billing split for sandbox cohort

Hi Alex —

Great chat this morning. Thanks for walking me through Lumen's cohort timeline. Two asks from our side to get procurement moving:

1) Escrow/transferability: you mentioned your finance team wants the sandbox grant held in escrow rather than applied as a direct account credit. We can support that, but need to confirm whether the escrowed credits should be tied to the company account or be transferable between startups in the cohort (you said there might be seat transfers).

2) Billing split & SLA exception: a quick edge case — a few of your founders will be experimenting with private deployment (VPC). That can change pricing units; if any usage runs through Dedicated nodes we may need an SLA exception and a one-off billing split in the contract.

I've attached a draft MOU and a sample credit schedule that maps grant amounts to enrollment milestones. Can you loop in your legal/finance and confirm:
- Whether escrow should allow intra-cohort transfers
- If the grant needs to be time-bound (expiration) or milestone-locked
- Any procurement paperwork template we should use for Lumen (PO, MSA addendum)

If helpful, Ben can walk through the accounting treatment and Marissa can propose a commercial carveout for private deployment usage.

Next step: can we get your legal ops on a 30-min call tomorrow afternoon?

Thanks —
Sean

Sean —

Thanks for the clear summary and the MOU. Quick answers from our side:

- Escrow: our finance team prefers the grant to be escrowed to Lumen's vendor account and then allocated to startups. We do expect transfers between cohort companies in limited cases (founder change or company acquisition). Is Redwood comfortable supporting controlled transfers with an audit trail?

- Time-bound vs milestones: we'd prefer a 12-month expiration from allocation to the startup, but cohort lead (Lumen) should be able to re-allocate unused credits after 6 months.

- Private deployment: a handful (~3–5) of founders will request VPC/Dedicated evaluation. We understand that shifts cost profile. We want a simple billing split: Redwood bills usage to Lumen for covered credits; any overages should be billed to the startup directly unless Lumen elects to cover them. Can you include a clause that flags Dedicated usage for separate invoicing?

Looping in Legal Ops (copied) — can you propose language for the transferability and re-allocation flow? Also CC'ing Priya from FounderHub since they want standardized wording for future cohorts.

—Alex

Marissa / team —

Quick finance/legal note after reviewing the proposed flow and talking to accounting:

1) Accounting treatment: If credits are escrowed on Lumen's vendor account and remain under Lumen's control until allocation, Redwood should treat the committed grant as a contractual liability rather than deferred revenue. Once credits are allocated to an end customer and consumed, we can recognize revenue. We'll need the allocation records exported monthly.

2) Transferability & audit trail: We can support controlled intra-cohort transfers but will require a signed transfer request form (digital signature acceptable) and a short 48-hour review window for compliance checks. We'll also log transfer events (who approved, timestamp, original allocation).

3) Dedicated usage carveout: Recommended clause — any usage that triggers Dedicated capacity should be invoiced separately and flagged as "Dedicated consumption" on the invoice. If Lumen elects to cover overages, they must notify Redwood within 30 days of the usage month for a credit application; otherwise usage will be billed to the startup.

Next steps: Irene, can you draft the 1-page addendum reflecting the above? Marissa, Sean — once we have that, I'll prepare an accounting appendix (monthly allocation export + transfer log schema) to attach to the MOU.

Ben
